newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber again closes mixed after new highs.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber again closes mixed after new highs.

text.p: CME lumber futures closed mixed after November and January again set new contract highs on support from apparent record-high cash prices, traders said.

November set a fresh high of $483.20 per thousand board feet and January, a new high of $428.40. Prices finished $2.80 per tbf higher to $7.00 lower with only November up at $482.80 and January off $0.40 at $425.00 per tbf.
Profit taking weighed on futures at various times and offset continued support from strong cash markets. Expectations are for cash to reach record highs, they said.

Current mill asking prices were running as high as $490 per tbf and sales were reported in the $475 to $480 area. This would likely be a new all time high price, traders said. The previous all time high spruce price was $475 posted in March, 1993, according to Random Lengths reporting service.

The surge in cash came following the announced company export quotas from Canada. Some mills have already exceeded their yearly export quota and pulled out of the market which sent cash prices soaring the past week, traders said.
However, deferred futures were weak on expected larger wood imports once the new quota year starts in Canada next spring, sources said.
